rows.why: No item asks whether a passing run releases the hidden-test share or what status follows. Item 9 covers which share values are valid and their unit, and item 1 covers rounding. Neither one settles the basic release that S1 checks.

Item 1 asks how a fractional split is rounded. Its pick rounds the hidden-test amount down and gives the leftover to UAT, and the call showed splitBounty(101,7500) → 75/26. That matches 999 → 749/250, with the two parts adding up to the bounty.
Item 10 asks what the UAT release amount equals. Its pick is bounty minus prior releases, and the call returned status 'fully released' with the remaining balance recorded.
Item 6 asks what a failed hidden-test run does. The call returned { status: 'locked', releases: [] } after the failure event, so nothing was recorded. Item 12 shows the same result with zero writes.
Item 2 asks what happens if UAT is approved before the hidden tests pass. The call threw 'cannot release on UAT approval: the hidden tests have not passed' and nothing was recorded.
Item 7 asks how a zero bounty is treated. The status is 'pro bono' as expected, but the call recorded zero-amount releases for both hidden-tests and uat. S6 says no release is ever recorded.

Item 3 asks what happens when the hidden tests pass a second time, whether a duplicate or a re-run. Its pick ignores the repeat and records no new release, and the second result matched the first. The call made two writes only because its test store never kept what was saved. Item 4 used a store that keeps state, and there the repeat caused no extra write.

Item 5 asks how duplicate or concurrent events are handled and whether event id is used. Its pick queues events per handler and dedupes by release kind, so different ids are covered too. The concurrent call with a delayed store made exactly one write and one release.
No item asks what happens when the store rejects a save, or whether the event can then be retried. Item 12 only covers when writes happen and what the initial state is.
